Hi Marissa —

Thanks — great demo. Quick answers below from our side:

1) Token volumes (monthly, prod):
- Current prod estimate (phase 1): ~700M tokens/month (mix of prompts + generated tokens).
- Expected growth (12 months): 1.5B–2B tokens/month if we roll out to all regions.

2) Budget:
- Initial pilot budget target: $15k–$25k/month.
- If economics work, procurement has room up to $40k–$50k/month in Q3/Q4 depending on SLA and support.

3) Latency / SLOs:
- p95 target: <= 250ms for most read-only recommendation requests; some personalization flows can tolerate up to 500ms. Peak concurrent QPS: ~200–300 during spikes.

Caching question:
We see lots of repeated prefixes (search/autocomplete and cart contexts). Our BAU estimate is 30%–45% prefix repetition (so hoping for 30%–45% cache hit on inputs). Curious how that maps to effective cost at your baseline unit price.

Hi Sam —

Quick technical note on how we model caching in pricing and an example calculation so you can see the sensitivity. High-level: prefix caching primarily reduces the number of input (prompt) tokens that need to be sent to the model; KV/prefix cache works best for deterministic or repeated prefixes (search/autocomplete, templated product descriptions). It does not change the number of output/generated tokens if your application requires new completions each time.

Assumptions we typically use for pricing exercises:
- Baseline unit price (hosted example): $15.00 per 1M billed tokens (prompt+completion).
- Cache hit definition: percentage of input tokens satisfied from cache so those tokens are not sent to model (hence not billed).
- For many retail workloads we conservatively model prefix cache hit rates in the 25%–50% band; 30%–45% is reasonable for autocomplete/search.

Example math (simple):
- Observed tokens for a given month = 1,000,000 tokens (this includes both input prompt tokens and generated tokens).
- If 40% of input tokens are hits and inputs represent 60% of observed tokens (common when prompts are larger than outputs for recommendation templates), the billed tokens = observed_tokens - (input_tokens * hit_rate).
  - input_tokens = 1,000,000 * 0.6 = 600,000
  - saved_tokens = 600,000 * 0.40 = 240,000
  - billed_tokens = 1,000,000 - 240,000 = 760,000
  - billed cost at $15/1M = (760,000 / 1,000,000) * $15 = $11.40
  - effective $/1M observed tokens = $11.40 (i.e., you effectively pay $11.40 for the original 1M tokens before caching)

If inputs are a smaller % of total (say 40% input / 60% output) and the hit rate is 30%:
- input_tokens = 1,000,000 * 0.4 = 400,000
- saved = 400,000 * 0.30 = 120,000
- billed = 880,000 -> cost = $13.20 per 1M observed

Key takeaways:
- Effective $/1M observed tokens depends on 3 things: baseline price, fraction of tokens that are inputs vs generated, and prefix cache hit rate.
- Small increases in hit rate (e.g., 30% -> 45%) can meaningfully lower effective cost. In the first example above, moving from 40% -> 50% input hit reduces billed tokens to 700k -> cost $10.50 per 1M observed.

Caveats and operational notes:
- Prefix caching helps most for deterministic or templated prompts. For large open-ended generation (long generative descriptions), gains are limited.
- We can instrument a short pilot (2–4 weeks) to measure actual input repetition and provide an empirical hit-rate distribution rather than relying on heuristics. That’s the fastest way to get to your target economics.

Happy to walk through a slide or two in the workshop showing sensitivity curves.

— Marcus Lin

Thanks Sam — this is perfect. Based on the numbers you provided and Marcus' examples, quick notes and suggested next steps: 

1) Pilot scope & acceptance criteria
- Pilot period: 4 weeks; target observed tokens: 200M (prod-like traffic window).
- Success metrics: empirical prefix cache hit >= 35%, effective $/1M observed tokens <= $12 for pilot.

2) Pricing options to align with your budget band ($15k–$25k/mo):
- Hosted baseline ($15/1M billed): with an expected 35% input hit and inputs ~60% of tokens, rough effective = ~$12.75/1M observed. That maps to ~15k for ~1.2M observed? (we'll run the full table in the workshop)
- Dedicated/reserved discount: we can introduce committed throughput pricing that brings baseline to $10–12/1M billed depending on commit and term — which after caching gets you comfortably into the $8–$10 effective band you mentioned for $40k+ budgets.

3) Next week workshop: Tue 4/6 11am PT confirmed. Agenda: walkthrough MAP, run hit-rate sensitivity on your sample CSV (attached), and outline pilot MOPs + telemetry we need (trace IDs, sample prompts, success criteria).

4) Attachments & docs
- I re-attached the cache assumptions and the MAP. Please add your token volume numbers to the MAP sheet and we’ll produce the sensitivity tables pre-call.

If procurement needs a separate thread for terms, feel free to loop them in — we flagged a preliminary deal in HubSpot (HS-123456).
